finding.summary: start_queued returns after the first exception from loop.start, so a ticket that consistently fails to start (e.g. bad folder, tmux unavailable) blocks all subsequent queued tickets indefinitely — the queue starves.
finding.fix: Instead of returning, continue to the next queued ticket, or implement a retry limit/backoff so one failing ticket cannot starve the queue. Consider skipping the failed ticket and trying the next one, then retrying failed tickets on subsequent ticks.

label: false_positive
label_reason: a refused tab is almost always tmux itself, which fails every ticket alike; the one per-ticket cause (its repo folder deleted while queued) is shown in red every check, and skipping it would break the owner's command-line order.
notes: finding.line moved 159 -> 158: at raised_sha c3e9e57 the `return` after the exception the finding describes is at cli.py:158 (159 is the started event); the review cited the wrong line.
